title: Central Maintenance System — Crew Interface and Configuration Reporting
abstract: Flight crew description of the central maintenance system, what the crew can see of the aeroplane software configuration, and how a maintenance action left incomplete before departure appears on the flight deck.

sections.purpose: This entry describes the central maintenance system as the flight crew sees it, and explains what a maintenance status displayed before departure means for the crew.
sections.description: The central maintenance system collects the reports raised by the aeroplane systems and presents them to maintenance through a terminal that is not part of the flight deck. The crew sees only a summary status, which indicates whether maintenance action is outstanding. The system also holds a record of the aeroplane software configuration and of the loading actions carried out on it. A loading action that was started and not completed leaves the record showing an incomplete entry, and the aeroplane displays a maintenance status until the record has been resolved. The crew cannot resolve this status from the flight deck and must not attempt to clear it; it is not a system failure and does not by itself affect any aeroplane function, but the configuration of the affected system is not confirmed until maintenance has closed the record.
sections.crew_procedure: Before departure, check the maintenance status on the systems page. If a status is displayed and the technical log carries no corresponding entry, contact maintenance before accepting the aeroplane. Do not attempt to clear a maintenance status from the flight deck. If a loading action has been carried out during the turnaround, confirm with maintenance that the record has been closed and that the technical log entry is signed before departure.

type_data.crew_action: Check the maintenance status before departure; do not clear it from the flight deck.
